name: playground-clapping-drill
style: UK drill, 142 bpm, cold and menacing, dark London drill instrumental with sparse broken skippy hi-hats, kick and snare at half the hat rate, gliding sliding 808 sub that bends between notes, an eerie two-note minor bell motif looping over and over, dry low-end-heavy mix. On top, NOT a rapper: a small gang of real ten-year-old British schoolkids, 5 or 6 of them in unison, unpolished and imperfect, chanting a hand-clapping playground rhyme in a sing-song lilt, half-spoken, bored and deadpan with a stifled giggle, flat South London kid accents. Real palm-on-palm hand claps in the clapping-game pattern and a skipping rope slapping tarmac on every beat, recorded outdoors close and dry. The kids sound like they are in a different, sunnier song than the beat. Four lines, then the beat cuts dead.
exclude: piano, organ, harmonium, adult vocals, male rapper, choir, church reverb, hall reverb, strings swell, autotune, melodic R&B hook, fade out
lyrics:
[Intro: drill beat drops in, one bar, rope slapping tarmac]

[Playground clapping rhyme, kids in unison, sing-song, half-chanted]
We can't afford a bed for you,
The purse is far too thin;
[Clap clap, a giggle swallowed]
There is room on all those islands,
But you will sleep in a bin.

[Beat stops dead]
[End]
